bug_semantics: Xext/sync.c SyncChangeCounter walks a SyncCounter trigger list by caching pnext = ptl->next, then may invoke pTrigger->TriggerFired. For an XSync Await group that callback is SyncAwaitTriggerFired, which FreeResource()s the Await; FreeAwait then deletes every sibling wait-condition trigger from its SyncObject (SyncDeleteTriggerFromSyncObject, historically SyncDeleteTriggerFromCounter), unlinking and freeing list nodes that can include the cached pnext. The next loop step is therefore a use-after-free (CWE-416). A local client that places multiple Await conditions on counters, then has those counters change (including via a second client), can crash the X server or escalate if it runs as root. The 2026 patch restarts iteration from pTriglist when pnext is no longer on the list.
flaw_origin: The unsafe iterator and the Await-fire path that frees sibling trigger-list nodes first appear together in public xserver git as ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 (2003-11-14, Kaleb Keithley, "R6.6 is the Xorg base-line"). That commit adds Xext/sync.c containing SyncChangeCounter's for (ptl = pCounter->pTriglist; ptl; ptl = pnext) { pnext = ptl->next; if (CheckTrigger) TriggerFired; } loop, SyncAwaitTriggerFired calling FreeResource on the Await, and FreeAwait calling SyncDeleteTriggerFromCounter for each wait condition. Immediate parent cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941 has no Xext/sync.c (tree is only hw/). Later c66a410d378090f350beb398649e9d9262933785 (generic SyncObject rename), 9838b7032ea9792bec21af424c53c07078636d21 (indent-only), 2523a445a09a75a8baf642608d099a5e12d5437f (SyncUpdateCounter split), and e0f872207aa203adb85e825c311ed50fe3a3af60 (CARD64 to int64_t) keep the same pnext cache and fire path; they are not first-writes. The 2003 commit is a vendor import/baseline rather than a reconstructable squash of finer public members; no finer public object first writing these lines was found.

reasoning: Vulnerability first: the advisory names a SyncChangeCounter use-after-free when Await triggers fire and sibling list nodes are freed; the pre-fix loop caches pnext across TriggerFired, and 2003 SyncAwaitTriggerFired already FreeResource()s the Await so FreeAwait deletes sibling nodes, which is the CWE-416. The 2026 patch does not change CheckTrigger/TriggerFired semantics; it only restarts the iterator, confirming the defect is the unsafely cached next pointer. Style, type, and SyncObject-generic refactors are not first-writes. The baseline is the smallest surviving public object; no finer public member reconstructing the same first-write was found.
